primary_claim: Self-Other Overlap (SOO) fine-tuning substantially reduces deceptive responses in LLMs (e.g. Mistral-7B-Instruct 73.6%->17.2%, Gemma-2-27b-it 100%->9.3%, CalmeRys-78B-Orpo-v0.1 100%->2.7%) with minimal impact on general performance, whereas simply prompting the models to be honest did not reduce deception.

effect.metric: deceptive response rate, baseline vs. after SOO fine-tuning

stated_future_work: rigorously testing the limits and generalizability of this approach
exploring its long-term effects on model behavior
improve generalization by incorporating a broader range of scenarios and fine-tuning variations
integration of SOO fine-tuning with other alignment methods, such as Constitutional AI or RLHF
limitations_stated: the current fine-tuning process has limited variability and does not yet cover the full range of fine-tuning configurations that could be explored in larger-scale experiments
SOO fine-tuning achieved almost no reduction in deception for Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 in the 'Treasure Hunt' scenario
effectiveness of SOO fine-tuning's generalization varies by scenario
MT-Bench capability score showed a slight decrease for Gemma-2-27b-it (8.81 to 8.4) and CalmeRys-78B-Orpo (8.96 to 8.5)
quote: Our results show that Self-Other Overlap (SOO) fine-tuning substantially reduces deceptive responses in LLMs with minimal impact on general performance across the scenarios we evaluated.
